note: Recast from the original description of Emerson (1928), original in English; the holotype is a soldier (American Museum of Natural History), the description based on 4 major soldiers and 1 minor soldier (the latter from the stomach contents of Arthroleptus variabilis), with workers also included. The alate is not recorded. Synonymic citations, distribution records and figure numbers are not translated. Line-end hyphenation of the original has been joined.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Major soldier: head reddish yellow, the sides almost straight and parallel; antennal segment 3 longer than 4 and shorter than 2; a black eye-spot behind the base of the antenna; labrum with several long bristles, reaching the teeth of the left mandible when the mandibles are closed; mandibles deep reddish brown, paler at the base; anterior margin of the pronotum distinctly concave. Measurements (mm): head length 3.20—3.21, head width 1.51, pronotum length 0.58—0.61, pronotum width 0.96, hind tibia length 1.19, left mandible length 1.12. Minor soldier: the original considers it possibly only a variation of the major soldier rather than a separate caste. Head length 2.90, head width 1.28, pronotum width 0.87, hind tibia length 1.12, left mandible length 0.96 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Antenna 17 segments; head width 1.45 mm. The original gives no other description.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Very close to T. pauperans Silvestri, but the sides of the head are more parallel, the anterior narrowing is less pronounced than in that species, and the labrum can reach the teeth of the left mandible. Silvestri examined specimens of this species and regarded it merely as a variety of T. stercorivorus; but the sides of the head are more strongly curved in T. stercorivorus. The syntype soldiers of T. tanganicus are distinctly larger, although among Silvestri's material one soldier in the same vial approaches or even matches this species, which the original author attributes to a mixing of specimens.
